title: Da or når for when
goal: Choose da for one specific past time and når for future or repeated time.

objectives.statement: Choose da for one specific past time and når for future or repeated time.

spans.value: Mina has recently moved to Bergen. On Monday morning, she tells her colleague Jonas about the weekend.
Da jeg kom hjem på fredag, lå det en melding fra tante Liv på telefonen.

blocks.translation: When I came home on Friday, there was a message from Aunt Liv on my phone.

spans.value: Hva ville hun?
Hun inviterte meg på middag. Når hun får besøk, lager hun alltid altfor mye mat.

blocks.translation: She invited me to dinner. When she has visitors, she always makes far too much food.

spans.value: Det høres hyggelig ut.
Ja. Da jeg kom dit på lørdag, sto det fire retter på bordet.

blocks.translation: Yes. When I arrived there on Saturday, there were four dishes on the table.

spans.value: Fire retter for to personer?
Selvfølgelig! Når vi spiser sammen, sender hun alltid rester med meg hjem.

blocks.translation: Of course! When we eat together, she always sends leftovers home with me.

spans.value: Så nå har du middag hele uka?

blocks.translation: So now you have dinner for the whole week?

spans.value: Nesten. Og når hun kommer til meg neste måned, skal jeg lage middag til henne.

blocks.translation: Almost. And when she comes to my place next month, I’m going to make dinner for her.

spans.value: Mina uses English when several times in her story, but Norwegian divides these situations between
da
and
når
. The important question is not simply whether the sentence is in the past, present, or future. You must ask what kind of time Mina means.
She uses
da
for one specific occasion in the past: coming home on Friday and arriving at her aunt’s home on Saturday. She uses
når
for things that happen repeatedly and for her aunt’s future visit.

sections.title: One English word, two Norwegian choices

spans.value: In this lesson,
da
and
når
introduce a time clause: a part of a sentence that tells us when something happens.
Use this compact rule:

items.value: for one specific time or event in the past.
for future time or repeated time.

spans.value: A traditional memory aid is:

no.value: Den gang da, hver gang når.

en.value: That one time: da. Every time: når.

spans.value: This means roughly:
That one time: da. Every time: når.
The memory aid is useful, but the real decision is about meaning. Is the speaker pointing to one completed past occasion, or to a future or recurring situation?
Look again at Mina’s first sentence:

no.value: Da jeg kom hjem på fredag, lå det en melding på telefonen.

en.value: When I came home on Friday, there was a message on my phone.

no.value: Da jeg kom dit på lørdag, sto det fire retter på bordet.

en.value: When I arrived there on Saturday, there were four dishes on the table.

spans.value: Friday’s arrival happened once. Mina is describing one definite point in her past, so she uses
da
The same applies to her arrival at Aunt Liv’s home:
The expressions på fredag and på lørdag make the specific occasions especially clear. However, a sentence does not need an exact date to use
da
. The wider context may already identify one particular past event.

no.value: Da bussen stoppet, gikk vi av.

en.value: When the bus stopped, we got off.

no.value: Jeg ble overrasket da jeg så henne.

en.value: I was surprised when I saw her.

no.value: Da møtet var ferdig, ringte jeg pappa.

en.value: When the meeting was over, I called Dad.

spans.value: Each sentence presents one completed situation. There was one bus stop in the event being described, one sight of the woman, and one end to the meeting.
The
da
clause can come before or after the other part of the sentence:

no.value: Da filmen begynte, slo alle av telefonene.

en.value: When the film started, everyone turned off their phones.

no.value: Alle slo av telefonene da filmen begynte.

en.value: Everyone turned off their phones when the film started.

spans.value: The position changes what comes first in the sentence, but it does not change the choice of
da
. The film began on one specific past occasion.
Now compare Mina’s description of her aunt’s usual behavior:

no.value: Når hun får besøk, lager hun alltid altfor mye mat.

en.value: When she has visitors, she always makes far too much food.

no.value: Når vi spiser sammen, sender hun alltid rester med meg hjem.

en.value: When we eat together, she always sends leftovers home with me.

spans.value: Mina is not talking about only last Saturday. She means that this happens regularly. Every time Aunt Liv has visitors, she prepares too much food. Therefore Mina uses
når
Again, this is a recurring pattern. Words such as alltid, ofte, vanligvis and hver gang frequently help reveal repeated meaning.

no.value: Når jeg tar bussen, leser jeg nyhetene.

en.value: When I take the bus, I read the news.

no.value: Vi går ofte en tur når været er fint.

en.value: We often go for a walk when the weather is nice.

no.value: Når Erik lager middag, hører han på musikk.

en.value: When Erik makes dinner, he listens to music.

no.value: Barna blir glade når bestefar kommer på besøk.

en.value: The children are happy when Grandpa comes to visit.

spans.value: In each example, the speaker describes what normally happens in a recurring situation.
Repeated time can also be in the past. This is an important boundary because
da
does not simply mean past and
når
does not simply mean present or future.
Compare these two sentences:

no.value: Da jeg besøkte bestemor på søndag, bakte hun vafler.

en.value: When I visited Grandma on Sunday, she made waffles.

no.value: Når jeg besøkte bestemor, bakte hun alltid vafler.

en.value: When I visited Grandma, she always made waffles.

spans.value: The first sentence refers to one Sunday visit, so it uses
da
. The second describes a repeated pattern across several visits, so it uses
når
Another contrast:

no.value: Da toget kom i går, sto Anna på perrongen.

en.value: When the train arrived yesterday, Anna was standing on the platform.

no.value: Når toget kom om morgenen, sto Anna vanligvis på perrongen.

en.value: When the train arrived in the morning, Anna was usually standing on the platform.

spans.value: The verb forms are in the past in both pairs. The choice changes because the meaning changes: one occasion versus a repeated situation.
Mina ends her story by looking ahead:

no.value: Når hun kommer til meg neste måned, skal jeg lage middag til henne.

en.value: When she comes to my place next month, I’m going to make dinner for her.

no.value: Når jeg kommer hjem, skal jeg ringe deg.

en.value: When I get home, I’ll call you.

no.value: Vi spiser når de andre kommer.

en.value: We’ll eat when the others arrive.

no.value: Når kurset er ferdig, skal Amir ta en ferie.

en.value: When the course is finished, Amir is going to take a holiday.

no.value: Hun sender oss adressen når hun finner et hotell.

en.value: She’ll send us the address when she finds a hotel.

spans.value: The visit has not happened yet. Mina is talking about a future situation, so she uses
når
Notice that the Norwegian time clause often uses a present-tense form even though the meaning is future:

no.value: Når hun kommer, skal jeg lage middag.

en.value: When she comes, I’m going to make dinner.

spans.value: The future meaning comes from the whole sentence and its context. For the choice in this lesson, the key fact is simple: the event is expected later, so use
når
, not
da
The following sentences use similar vocabulary but describe different time relationships.
One specific past dinner

no.value: Da gjestene kom i går, serverte Liv suppa.

en.value: When the guests arrived yesterday, Liv served the soup.

spans.value: There was one arrival yesterday. Use
da
A repeated dinner routine

no.value: Når gjestene kommer, serverer Liv ofte suppe først.

en.value: When guests arrive, Liv often serves soup first.

spans.value: This describes Liv’s usual routine. Use
når
A future dinner

no.value: Når gjestene kommer i morgen, skal Liv servere suppe.

en.value: When the guests arrive tomorrow, Liv is going to serve soup.

spans.value: This refers to tomorrow. Use
når
The compact decision is therefore:
One specific completed past occasion → da
Future or repeated situation → når

sections.title: A common mistake: choosing from tense alone

spans.value: A learner may see a past-tense verb and automatically choose
da

no.value: Da jeg var liten, gikk jeg til skolen hver dag.

en.value: When I was little, I walked to school every day.

spans.value: This sentence can describe childhood as one overall period, so
da
is natural: during that specific period of my life.
But consider a sentence about repeated occasions inside childhood:

no.value: Når det snødde, tok vi alltid bussen til skolen.

en.value: When it snowed, we always took the bus to school.

spans.value: Here the meaning is every time it snowed. The repeated situations require
når
, even though both snødde and tok are past-tense forms.
Compare:

no.value: Da det snødde på mandag, tok vi bussen.

en.value: When it snowed on Monday, we took the bus.

no.value: Når det snødde, tok vi alltid bussen.

en.value: When it snowed, we always took the bus.

spans.value: The first sentence identifies one snowy Monday. The second describes a recurring response to snow.
Do not ask only, Is this sentence in the past? Ask:
Is this one particular past occasion, or something that happened repeatedly?

sections.title: Returning to Mina and Aunt Liv

spans.value: Later that day, Jonas asks Mina what she plans to cook for her aunt.
Hva skal du lage når tante Liv kommer?

blocks.translation: What are you going to make when Aunt Liv comes?

spans.value: Jeg vet ikke ennå. Da jeg spiste hos henne på lørdag, fikk vi fiskesuppe.

blocks.translation: I don’t know yet. When I ate at her place on Saturday, we had fish soup.

spans.value: Lager hun alltid fiskesuppe når du besøker henne?

blocks.translation: Does she always make fish soup when you visit her?

spans.value: Nei, hun lager noe forskjellig hver gang. Når jeg bestemmer meg, sender jeg henne menyen.

blocks.translation: No, she makes something different every time. When I decide, I’ll send her the menu.

spans.value: Jonas’s first question concerns a future visit, so he uses
når
. Mina then refers back to one particular Saturday meal and uses
da
. Jonas asks about a possible routine and uses
når
. Finally, Mina refers to a future decision and again uses
når
The same people and topic can therefore require both words. What matters is the time relationship intended in each sentence.
A small change in context can change the correct word.

no.value: Da Nora åpnet døra i går, sto det en pakke utenfor.

en.value: When Nora opened the door yesterday, there was a package outside.

no.value: Når Nora åpner døra om morgenen, slipper hun katten ut.

en.value: When Nora opens the door in the morning, she lets the cat out.

no.value: Når Nora åpner døra i morgen, vil hun se den nye navneplaten.

en.value: When Nora opens the door tomorrow, she will see the new nameplate.

spans.value: The physical action is similar in all three examples. The time meaning is different:

items.value: yesterday points to one past occasion;
in the morning describes a routine;

spans.value: You can create similar contrasts with common events:

no.value: Da jeg gikk av bussen, begynte det å regne.

en.value: When I got off the bus, it started to rain.

no.value: Når jeg går av bussen, kjøper jeg ofte kaffe.

en.value: When I get off the bus, I often buy coffee.

no.value: Når jeg går av bussen senere, skal jeg ringe deg.

en.value: When I get off the bus later, I’ll call you.

sections.title: Cumulative transfer: a new everyday situation

spans.value: Imagine that Sander is preparing for a driving lesson tomorrow. He remembers his first lesson, thinks about what normally happens during lessons, and makes plans for the next one.
He might need meanings such as these:

no.value: Da jeg kjørte for første gang, var jeg veldig nervøs.

en.value: When I drove for the first time, I was very nervous.

no.value: Når jeg blir nervøs, snakker kjørelæreren rolig.

en.value: When I get nervous, the driving instructor speaks calmly.

no.value: Når timen begynner i morgen, skal jeg huske å puste rolig.

en.value: When the lesson starts tomorrow, I’ll remember to breathe calmly.

spans.value: The topic has changed, but the decision remains the same. One first lesson in the past takes
da
. A recurring reaction takes
når
. Tomorrow’s lesson also takes
når
Complete a final three-part retrieval task about a new everyday event: one thing that happened on a specific past day, one thing that happens regularly, and one thing that will happen later. Choose
da
or
når
in each time clause and briefly state whether the meaning is specific past, repeated, or future.
Remember:
One specific past occasion: da. Future or repeated time: når.

prompt.value: Choose the interpretation that explains why the time word fits the single completed past event.

options.text: The clause describes a repeated routine every time I came home; the connector should be når, not da.
options.why: The sentence identifies one Friday arrival, not a recurring routine.

options.text: The clause Da jeg kom hjem på fredag describes one particular completed arrival on Friday; da is appropriate. (When I came home on Friday, there was a message on my phone.)
options.why: The Friday arrival is one identified, completed past occasion, so da fits.

options.text: The clause describes a future arrival; the connector should be når, not da.
options.why: The sentence describes a completed past arrival, not a future event.

stem.value: Read: Da jeg kom hjem på fredag, lå det en melding på telefonen. Choose the complete meaning of the time clause and connector.

prompt.value: Classify each sentence by its past-time meaning. Use one bucket per sentence; the bucket labels include the connector that matches the meaning.

explanation.value: Use da for one specific past occasion and når for events that happened repeatedly.

items.text: Da jeg besøkte bestemor på søndag, bakte hun vafler. (When I visited Grandma on Sunday, she made waffles.)
Når jeg besøkte bestemor, bakte hun alltid vafler. (When I visited Grandma, she always made waffles.)
Da toget kom i går, sto Anna på perrongen. (When the train arrived yesterday, Anna was standing on the platform.)
Når toget kom om morgenen, sto Anna vanligvis på perrongen. (When the train arrived in the morning, Anna was usually standing on the platform.)

prompt.value: Complete each future-time sentence with the correct taught time word. The later event after the comma sets the time for the main event.

explanation.value: Use når for a future time condition, followed by present tense in the subordinate clause.

spans.value: Item 1:
jeg kommer hjem neste uke, skal jeg ringe hotellet.
Item 2:
jeg avslutter arbeidet, skal jeg møte en venn.
Item 3:
kurset er ferdig, skal Amir besøke familien.

prompt.value: Classify each sentence as one specific past occasion, repeated time, or future time. The bucket also records the correct connector; classify by meaning rather than verb tense.

items.text: Da gjestene kom i går, serverte Liv suppa. (When the guests arrived yesterday, Liv served the soup.)
Når gjestene kommer, serverer Liv ofte suppe først. (When guests arrive, Liv often serves soup first.)
Når gjestene kommer i morgen, skal Liv servere suppe. (When the guests arrive tomorrow, Liv is going to serve soup.)

prompt.value: Correct the Norwegian sentence by changing the time word, then explain in Norwegian why the corrected word fits the repeated-past meaning.

criteria.instruction: Changes Da to Når in the sentence.
Explains in Norwegian that alltid signals repeated past conditions rather than one specific occasion.

prompt.value: Complete the connected account with the correct taught time word in each blank. Use the time expressions and routine marker to distinguish one past occasion, repeated time, and future time.

spans.value: Mina forteller om tante Liv:
Mina kom til tante Liv på lørdag, fikk de fiskesuppe.
Mina besøker tante Liv, lager tante Liv alltid noe nytt. Neste måned skal Mina bestemme menyen.
Mina bestemmer menyen, skal hun sende tante Liv en melding.

prompt.value: Rewrite this sentence in two ways while keeping the basic event: Da jeg kom hjem på fredag, ringte jeg pappa. (When I came home on Friday, I called Dad.) First write a repeated routine with når; then write a future plan with når. Adjust tense or time expressions naturally.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the two Norwegian sentences against the task and report evidence for each criterion. Accept natural tense and time-expression changes, but require the requested connector choices.

criteria.instruction: Writes a repeated-time version of the arrival-and-call event and uses **når**.
Writes a future-time version of the arrival-and-call event and uses **når**.
Keeps the basic arrival-and-call event in both rewrites while changing the time meaning.

prompt.value: Write a short connected account in Norwegian about Sander’s driving lessons. Include one sentence for each cue: one specific earlier lesson, something that normally happens during lessons, and tomorrow’s lesson or plan. Use da for the single past occasion and når for both the routine and future plan. Use your own wording.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the connected Norwegian account against the task and report evidence for each criterion. Require meaning-based use of da and når, not tense-only matching.

criteria.instruction: Describes one specific completed earlier driving lesson and uses **da** for its time clause.
Describes something that normally happens during driving lessons and uses **når**.
Describes tomorrow’s driving lesson or plan and uses **når**, even if the time clause uses present tense.
Connects all three contexts in one short account with original wording.
